decisions.title: RuntimeTaskRecord Separate from Task Goal
decisions.description: The durable task goal stays on the board while each live execution gets its own RuntimeTaskRecord with id, status, started_at, result_preview, and output_file. The record describes one execution attempt, not the task goal itself. This separation means a task can be retried without losing the original goal, and the runtime can track execution independently from planning.
decisions.alternatives: Reusing the task record for execution status conflates goal and attempt, making retries ambiguous. A single shared execution slot per task prevents concurrent attempts but limits throughput.

decisions.title: Preview in Notification, Full Output on Disk
decisions.description: Background task results split into two layers: a short preview sent through the notification queue, and the full output written to a file. The main loop learns what happened from the preview without flooding its context. If the model needs detail, it reads the file. This keeps context manageable even when background tasks produce large outputs.
decisions.alternatives: Sending the full output through the notification queue would flood the context window. Writing only to disk means the main loop has to proactively check files for results. The preview+file split gives immediate awareness with optional detail.

decisions.title: Notifications Rejoin the Main Loop, Not a Second Loop
decisions.description: Background threads do not mutate model state directly. They write runtime records and notifications, then the next turn injects them into context. The main loop remains the single state machine. Background execution only adds parallelism to waiting, not parallelism to reasoning.
decisions.alternatives: Allowing background threads to modify the conversation directly creates race conditions. A second parallel loop would be a second agent, not a background task. The notification bridge keeps the architecture simple.
